description: Design, build, and ship large software systems. Focus on requirements, architecture, testing, and team delivery.

electives.reason: Requirements are the starting point of every real system; this is the core skill for a software engineer.
System architecture decides whether a codebase survives growth; essential for senior engineering roles.
Hands-on construction skills: frameworks, APIs, and build tooling used daily in industry.
Project management and Agile delivery — the difference between shipping and stalling.
User-centred design makes products people can actually use.
Web development is the most common first job; this covers the full stack.

name: Software Engineering

description: Protect systems, networks, and data. Focus on networking, operating systems, cryptography, and secure design.

electives.reason: You cannot secure a network you do not understand; protocols and routing come first.
The dedicated security course: threat models, cryptography, and secure design.
Low-level architecture knowledge is what separates security engineers from script users.
Most attacks target the web; understanding web architecture is a security prerequisite.
Databases hold the data attackers want; know how they are built and protected.

name: Cybersecurity

description: Build systems that learn and reason. Focus on algorithms, probability, linear algebra, and data at scale.

electives.reason: The core AI course: search, reasoning, and machine learning fundamentals.
Algorithms are the engine of AI; analysis skills transfer directly to model design.
Probability is the language of machine learning.
AI runs on data; advanced databases teach you to manage it at scale.
Linear algebra underpins neural networks and embeddings.

name: Artificial Intelligence

description: Turn data into decisions. Focus on databases, statistics, and communicating findings.

electives.reason: Advanced databases: how to store, query, and process large datasets.
Statistical inference is the foundation of every data analysis.
Applied statistics for real-world data questions.
Relational databases and SQL — the daily tool of every data role.
Probability theory behind distributions, sampling, and A/B testing.
Machine learning is the natural next step after statistics.

name: Data Science
